subject: Re: FlashHealth renewal — options for mid-contract top-up and term alignment
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@flashhealth.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Cooper <m.cooper@flashhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Need pricing for immediate top-up + align term

Hi Soojin,

Quick one — we have a product launch in June and are forecasting an additional ~200k tokens/month starting 6/1 for at least the next 6 months. Current committed baseline is 2M tokens/month under our existing SOW (runs through 12/31/2026).

Can you outline the simplest path to add the extra capacity immediately and any pricing impact if we instead annualize that extra usage and move to a contract term that syncs with our year-end (co-term to 12/31/2026)?

Two constraints: procurement needs a rough TCO estimate this week, and legal prefers minimal amendments rather than a full SOW rewrite. Marcus and I are looped.

Thanks — appreciate a couple of concrete options with numbers.

Samantha Ortiz
VP Product
FlashHealth
From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@flashhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need pricing for immediate top-up + align term

Thanks for the details, Samantha — congrats on the launch. I copied Rishi (pricing) and Laura (billing) to help scope options. Attached a quick usage export you can confirm against your numbers.

High level — two pragmatic paths we commonly recommend:

Option 1 — Add-on top-up (fastest):
- We add a monthly add-on for the extra 200k tokens starting 6/1, invoiced pro-rata for May/June if needed.
- Pricing: list price for tokens with a one-time 12% top-up discount for the duration of the spike (3–6 months typical).
- No term change; minimal paperwork (amendment).

Option 2 — Annualize + term synchronization (better unit economics):
- Convert the uplift into a temporary committed band and annualize it against a co-terminating amendment that ends 12/31/2026.
- Pricing: blended discount of 20% on the incremental band if FlashHealth commits to annualize and accept monthly true-ups.
- Requires a short amendment to the SOW and a DocuSign for signature.

Questions to help pick the right path:
- Is the uplift steady (200k/mo for 6 months) or front-loaded into the first 2–3 months?
- Do you want us to draft the amendment and the pro-rata invoice so procurement can review this week?

Attachments: usage_report_q1.csv (attached)

If you want firm numbers I can ask Rishi to run the banded math and produce a clean comparison (monthly invoice impact + annualized). Laura — can you confirm how a Dec co-term would be handled for billing/proration?

Best,
Sooj
Soojín Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@flashhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need pricing for immediate top-up + align term

Adding the numbers here so Samantha has something concrete for procurement. Assumptions: 200k extra tokens/month, baseline 2M/month, pricing band breakpoints tied to effective monthly committed tokens.

Suggested approach (ballpark numbers):
- Add-on path (Option 1):
  * List price increment for 200k = $1,800/month (example list numbers). With a 12% add-on discount = $1,584/month. Pro-rata first invoice if mid-month. No term change.
- Annualize & sync term (Option 2):
  * If FlashHealth annualizes the uplift and co-terms to 12/31/2026 (6–8 months remaining depending on start), we can offer a blended 20% discount on the incremental band. Equivalent monthly exposure approx $1,440/month, with the upside of predictable unit price and eligibility for volume credits.

Recommendation: If the uplift is >4 months, Option 2 is usually cheaper and reduces mid-contract administrative work. If it's a short, 1–2 month spike, Option 1 minimizes legal friction.

Operational notes:
- For Option 2 we will draft a 1-page amendment (amend SOW Appendix A) and route via DocuSign. Legal will accept the amendment rather than a full SOW rewrite.
- For Option 1 billing team will issue a one-line add-on invoice; procurement can pay via standard PO referencing the amendment ID.

Laura — can you confirm the billing delta (proration example) so I can include an example invoice line for procurement?

Rishi
Senior Manager, Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@flashhealth.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Cooper <m.cooper@flashhealth.com>, procurement@flashhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-06T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need pricing for immediate top-up + align term

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what procurement wanted to see. FlashHealth prefers Option 2 (annualize + sync to 12/31/2026) under the following conditions:
- Blended 20% discount on the incremental band while we commit to monthly true-ups and a 12-month lookback credit if usage undershoots by >15% over the first 3 months.
- Minimal paperwork: one-page amendment to the existing SOW and DocuSign routing to our procurement contact (procurement@flashhealth.com).

Next steps from our side: I'll confirm the exact start date for the uplift (likely 2026-06-01) and share an internal PO number by EOD Monday. Please send the amendment and DocuSign link. Also include the sample invoice proration so my finance team can reconcile the monthly P&L.

Thanks again — looping in Marcus for a final procurement nod.

Samantha Ortiz
VP Product, FlashHealth
